clue.text: Thoughtful study given incidental regard

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a side issue is an incidental one, so side can stand for incidental
to rate something is to regard or esteem it

explanation.surface: A careful scholar pays passing attention to some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person who keeps others' feelings in mind is said to be thoughtful.

clue.text: A brave appeal to one of great wisdom

parts.note: O is the vocative cry used in appeals, as in 'O Lord'
a sage is a very wise person

explanation.surface: Someone calls on a wise elder for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people, so a warrior of theirs is a brave.

clue.text: Various people taking the plunge

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning several or sundry

explanation.surface: Assorted folk jumping into the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry, and the plural noun means swimmers who jump in head first.

clue.text: Push the sailor's hammock for a season

parts.note: to rock is to push to and fro, as one does a hammock
an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: Swaying a seaman's hammock for a whole season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammock' just supports the picture of rocking; 'for a season' is a verb, something used to season food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salt is coarse mineral salt used to flavour food.

clue.text: Chest displayed by lofty young male

parts.note: lofty means tall
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A tall youth shows off his torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' suggests the body but is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a high chest of drawers.

clue.text: Palm found in employee's apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
a hand is a worker, so belonging to the employee is 'of the hand'

explanation.surface: A palm tree spotted in a worker's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is the inner surface of the hand between wrist and fingers.

clue.text: Profit declared and denied

parts.note: a gain is a profit
said means declared

explanation.surface: Someone claims a profit yet denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or refuse, so gainsaid is denied.

clue.text: Memories about Oxford college examinations

parts.note: re means about or concerning
collections are the internal exams set by Oxford colleges at the start of term

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces about their exams at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford, college exams taken at the start of term are called collections.
explanation.definitionFit: Recollections are things remembered from the past.

clue.text: Allowed to hold Roman coin of the smallest value

indicators.note: to hold means the word for allowed wraps round the coin

parts.note: allowed means let
the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Someone was permitted to keep a cheap Roman coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The as was the lowest-value copper coin of Rome, which suits the surface's 'smallest value'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of minimal worth is worth the least of all.

clue.text: I shall occupy empty premises despite waver

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so these letters go within the word for emptying premises

parts.note: to vacate premises is to empty them
taken as written
'I shall' contracts to I'LL, so shall gives LL

explanation.surface: Someone moves into an empty building though still unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: I'LL (I shall) goes inside VACATE; 'despite' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to hesitate between options, which is what wavering means.

clue.text: Reference book confirms that the aurochs consumed it

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so the beast's letters close round the small word

parts.note: taken as written
the urus is another name for the aurochs, an extinct wild ox
it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A reference work vouches that an extinct wild ox ate something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a crossword convention for sex appeal; 'confirms that' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book of synonyms that writers consult, so a reference book.

clue.text: Don't let Miss Durie in to play it!

parts.note: to ban is to not let something happen
Jo Durie was a leading British tennis player of the 1980s

explanation.surface: A plea to keep a tennis star out of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo Durie was Britain's top woman tennis player in the 1980s; 'in' is a link, and 'play it' reads as letting her play tennis but means an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, something a musician plays.

clue.text: French policeman taken to Kansas cinema

parts.note: flic is French slang for a policeman
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: A Paris gendarme is brought to a picture house in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: The flicks is informal British slang for the movies, so the cinema.

clue.text: Case revealing modish attitude of mind

parts.note: in means fashionable
a stance is a mental attitude or position

explanation.surface: A trial revealing a trendy outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example, as in 'a case in point'.

clue.text: Cooperate to produce a dramatic dance

parts.note: a play is a dramatic work
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Putting on a theatrical dance performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce a' links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work along with others.

clue.text: Alarming disturbance on the border

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worrying unrest along the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edge or margin of something.

clue.text: Talks given by Henry Briggs and Tom French

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Asa Briggs was a well-known British historian
a tom is a male cat, and the French for cat is chat

explanation.surface: A list of people giving lectures, as if on a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Asa Briggs was a famous British historian; 'Tom French' is a tom cat in French, CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has a chat is conversing, which is what talks means here.

clue.text: Money order registered by one on board

parts.note: a cheque is an order to pay money
R is the abbreviation for registered

explanation.surface: A payment sent by recorded post by a director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one on board' suggests a director or passenger; it is a draughts piece. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a counter used in draughts, played on a board.

clue.text: Some minor dictator from Scandinavia

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A petty tyrant who comes from northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the peoples and lands of northern Europe, including Scandinavia.

clue.text: On receiving small computer, produce circular letter in Greek

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the computer goes inside the short word

parts.note: taken as written
a micro is a microcomputer

explanation.surface: Getting a laptop to produce a mailshot in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circular letter' looks like a mailshot but is the round Greek letter O. 'produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the Greek alphabet's short O, which is round in shape.

clue.text: Look into the winning of every trick in a ski race

indicators.note: into means the word for look goes inside the card term

parts.note: in bridge, a grand slam is winning every trick
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Investigating a card game during a skiing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Slalom is a downhill skiing event zigzagging between poles.

clue.text: Pull up for man at side of road

indicators.note: at the side of means placed next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: A motorist stops to pick up a man waiting by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' looks like stopping a car; it means to haul upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave something is to lift or haul it with great effort.

clue.text: Irritate one president refining oil in Turkey

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or vex
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: refining oil reworks it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tetchy head of state oversees an oil refinery in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refining' rearranges OIL to OLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is a peninsula and town in Turkey, famous for the 1915 campaign.

clue.text: Where brothers are in command

definitions.meaning: monks or friars belong to a religious brotherhood

explanation.surface: Monks in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious community of friars, and an instruction given by authority.

clue.text: Refusal to go around in California by night

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: in means the piece for going round sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: to turn is to go around

explanation.surface: Someone declines to drive round California after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal means happening or active during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Gas a Fellow of the Royal Academy

parts.note: RA is the abbreviation for the Royal Academy
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A painter wonders about a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an academician who talks too much ('gas'), but 'Gas' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive element which is a noble gas.

clue.text: Early contest put disorderly army in peril

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly organised army endangers itself in an opening battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link; the letters of ARMY IN PERIL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary is a heat or qualifying round held before the main event.
